title: One-step autologous cartilage regeneration versus two-step autologous chondrocyte implantation: A randomized controlled trial evaluating clinical, radiological and patient related outcomes
summary:
Focal cartilage defects of the knee joint are common among young and active patients and often lead to pain, swelling and loss of joint function. Additionally, because of the limited healing potential of articular cartilage, there is a high risk for the development of early osteoarthritis (joint degeneration). There are several surgical techniques for focal cartilage regeneration. In Germany, one of the most frequently used techniques is autologous chondrocyte implantation (ACI). For ACI, cartilage specimens are harvested during a first arthroscopic surgery, which are then sent to a laboratory for the isolation and cultivation of chondrocytes (cartilage cells). After 3 to 4 weeks these chondrocytes will be implanted into the defect area during a second surgery. Besides the disadvantage of the need for two surgeries, a further limitation of this technique are the relatively high costs.
An alternative procedure is minced cartilage implantation (MCI). For this technique only one surgery is needed, during which healthy cartilage from a less load-carrying area is harvested, minced and implanted into the defect zone. This one-step approach is considered cost-effective and easy to apply. 
To date, there are only few studies which have investigated clinical outcomes after MCI. In particular, a direct comparison with ACI is still missing. The aim of the present study is to investigate the clinical and radiological results after MCI in comparison with the results after ACI. By means of clinical examinations, questionnaires and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data will be collected in order to draw conclusions regarding the postoperative results.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Symptomatic cartilage defect of the knee (size 2.5-6 cm), Focal defect grade 3 or 4 according to the International Cartilage Repair Society (ICRS)
Exclusion criteria:
Systemic disease (Rheumatic disease, Diabetes etc.), Previous surgeries at the cartilage, menisci or ligaments of the knee, History of fractures or osteotomies of the lower extremities
